source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Being essentially identical to a core needle biopsy, without much meaningful distinction between the two procedures","B":"Rarely if ever being used as part of cancer diagnosis in current clinical practice","C":"Removing only a small tissue sample using a needle, rather than the entire lesion itself","D":"Removes the entire suspicious lesion or mass, providing both diagnostic and potentially therapeutic information"}}
source_row.rationale: An excisional biopsy removes the entire suspicious lesion or mass (rather than just a sample as with core needle biopsy), providing both diagnostic information and potentially therapeutic benefit if the entire lesion is successfully removed, distinct from the more limited sampling of a core needle biopsy.
source_row.source_detail: Distinction Between Core Needle and Excisional Biopsy
